Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

last adjective

final

also the last one, for the last time, final, when did you last …?

classical

Cato Agr. 5.5: postrēmus cubitum eat
Cic. Or. 50: alia prīma pōnet, alia postrēma (Lewis & Short)

postrēmus, postrēma, postrēmum

adjective, declension

last (in a series), hindmost

For the last time is postrēmum: hodiē postrēmum mē vidēs, you are seeing me for the last time today (Ter. And. 2.1.22, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ultimus, ultima, ultimum — last, final; farthest

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Liv. 21.4.8: ultimus cōnsertō proeliō excēdēbat; Ov. Met. 3.135: ultima … diēs; Traupman 315; Traupman 337

  • extrēmus, extrēma, extrēmum — last, at the end; outermost

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Hor. Ars 417: occupet extrēmum scabiēs; Verg. A. 5.196: extrēmōs pudeat rediisse; Traupman 315

  • novissimus, novissima, novissimum — last (to come, to speak), latest

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 5.56: quī ex iīs novissimus venit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 87: Cicero spoke last, Cicerō novissimus locūtus est; Traupman 337

    Varro says that in his youth some old men still avoided it as too new a word (Varr. LL 6.59, Lewis & Short).

  • extrēmum — for the last time

    adverb (the neuter of extrēmus) · also used · classical · Ov. Tr. 1.3.15: alloquor extrēmum maestōs abitūrus amīcōs (Lewis & Short s.v. exter); Traupman 394

Examples

  • occupet extrēmum scabiēs

    the itch take the last one! (last one there’s a rotten egg)Hor. Ars 417

  • prīmus cubitū surgat, postrēmus cubitum eat

    let him be the first to get up and the last to go to bedCato Agr. 5.5

  • prīnceps in proelium ībat, ultimus cōnsertō proeliō excēdēbat

    he was the first to go into battle and the last to leave it once it was joinedLiv. 21.4.8

  • Quandō novissimē tolūtim cursitāvistī?

    When did you last go jogging?Traupman 84

  • extrēmum

    for the last time (adverb)Traupman 394

See also last.
